entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Edward Lipiński was a Polish economist, intellectual, social critic and human rights advocate. During the almost seven decades of his career, he held a series of academic and government advisory positions, founded several organizations, published books and essays on economic policy. His works concerned business cycles, growth theory, history of economic thought and other areas of economics. Lipiński was a fighter for Polish independence and a socialist activist in the Second Polish Republic. In the Polish People's Republic, Lipiński was an influential Marxian economist and a long-term member of the communist party.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Marxist economist and socialist activist in Poland during the communist era, Lipiński's work influenced the country's economic policies and contributed to its post-war reconstruction. His writings on growth theory and business cycles remain relevant in contemporary Polish academia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent economist and human rights advocate in Poland during the mid-20th century, Lipiński's work on economic policy had significant regional impact, particularly through his influential Marxist thought within the communist party. His contributions to understanding business cycles and growth theory also informed broader discussions of socialism.
